claims.summary: On the event of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split, with rho a bounded measurable mollifier supported in the unit disc and L depending only on its sup norm: for every 1 <= j <= l_1, h = 2^(-j), and every Lipschitz G on [0,1]^2, the mollification S of the even reflection of G at scale h has |sum_i S(X_i) - N int S| <= L sqrt N (j^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)) ||grad G||_1, its cellwise sum at mesh h being at most 81 ||rho||_inf ||grad G||_1. For class functions at (4,4) whose larger partial is at least y >= e^16 where the gradient is nonzero and j <= j*(y), this is O(sqrt(N log N)), so the single-level class bound reduces to the remainder G - S. Against Lebesgue measure.
claims.assessment: Working proof: nabla S = rho_h * nabla G-hat, the pointwise bound |nabla S| <= ||rho||_inf h^(-2) times the gradient mass of the nine neighbouring cells, so Lambda_j(S) <= 81 ||rho||_inf ||grad G||_1; then lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split, and the gradient-mass bound of lem:dominant-level-split for (b).
claims.rationale: Decides the fourth route review's test: charging a smooth part on the partition by the local spacing overcharges functions smooth above that scale (a constant-spacing staircase by (log N)^(1/4)); mollifying at 2^(-j*(y)) bounds the smooth part of every class function whose larger partial is at least y >= e^16 where its gradient is nonzero, so its single-level case is the high-frequency remainder's, which for features thinner than that scale is about the function itself.
claims.next_action: Bound the remainder G - rho_h * G-hat at h = 2^(-j*(y)) on curve traces with weights, first for a staircase along curved graphs.

relationships: Applied to the mollified function, whose cellwise sum is bounded by its gradient mass.
Its gradient-mass bound 8 (log y)^(-1/4) and j*(y); unlike it, no thickness condition is needed for the smooth part.
Charging a smooth part on a fine partition with that lemma overcharges a constant-spacing staircase by a factor of order (log N)^(1/4).
The single-level case at (4,4) reduces to the remainder below the scale 2^(-j*(y)).
